title: Homologous parts tend to vary together

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Homologous parts tend to vary together

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Parts of the body that are homologous and alike early in embryonic development, such as left and right sides or fore and hind limbs, tend to vary in a correlated way.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The several parts of the body which are homologous, and which, at an early embryonic period, are alike, seem liable to vary in an allied manner

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter V, “Laws of Variation”; section “Correlation of growth.”. Scope: animals and plants with serially or bilaterally homologous parts

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch05-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The covariance prediction is clear and can be tested in available specimen and morphometric datasets. Coverage across plants, animals and homology types is limited, and developmental causation is not always identifiable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate within-individual and genetic covariance in size, shape or developmental perturbation among homologous bilateral or serial parts. Positive covariance exceeding that among nonhomologous matched parts supports the claim; independence or negative covariance refutes it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public morphology repositories often lack pedigrees needed for genetic covariance.

Shared mechanical use can correlate homologues without shared developmental variation.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.86
discriminating power: 0.73
analysis feasibility: 0.65
data adequacy: 0.45
data existence: 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Covariation of homologous parts is a direct statistic with a clear null, so the claim operationalizes cleanly. The measurements are scattered across morphometric studies and model-organism databases, with broad coverage only if new measurements are taken from existing images. Discrimination is good once the data are assembled, and assembly is the limiting step.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Within species, correlate measurements of serial and bilateral homologs and compare those correlations with correlations between non-homologous parts. Stronger covariation among homologs would confirm the claim; correlations indistinguishable from non-homologous pairs would refute it. Genetic correlations in model organisms are a second, mechanistic layer.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Measuring existing scans at comparative scale is months of work.

AVONET does not pair forelimb and hindlimb homologs across animals generally.

Within-species covariance matrices are published piecemeal, not as a global download.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

analysis feasibility: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.66
data existence: 0.52
operationalizability: 0.82
